title: Basic Circumference Measurement
content: **List of Contents** Basic Circumference Measurement Measure Circumference **Basic Circumference Measurement** \- Measure a circumference of an Avatar. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021847927/mceclip0.png) **Basic Circumference Measurement** tool from the 3D toolbar or navigate to Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Measurement ▶ **Basic Circumference Measurement.** ** Measure Circumference** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021847947/mceclip1.png) **Basic Circumference Measurement** tool from the 3D Toolbar. \- Left click the total of three times to measure the Avatar’s circumference. \- Click once to start the Circumference Measurement, then move the mouse and click again to assign the measurement direction. \- Hover the mouse over the purple line connecting the first and the second point and move the mouse to assign the circumference angle. \- When the desired circumference angle is achieved, left click to complete the Circumference Measurement. \- After establishing the first point of the circumference, hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to create the second and third point in a straight line. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for measuring the circumference of an Avatar using the Basic Circumference Measurement tool in the 3D environment.

title: Attach to Avatar Tape
content: **List of Contents** Attach to Avatar Tape Attach Pattern to Avatar Tape Detach Pattern from Avatar Tape **Attach to Avatar Tape** \- Attach Pattern outlines or Internal Lines to Avatar Tapes. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021908568/mceclip0.png) **Attach to Avatar Tape** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to Main Menu and select Avatar ▶ Avatar Tape ▶ **Attach to Avatar Tape.** ** Attach Pattern to Avatar Tape** \- To attach a Pattern to an Avatar Tape, you will need to click the part of Pattern to be attached to the Avatar and the Avatar Tape. \- In the 3D window, click on the Pattern outline or the Internal Line to be attached to the Avatar. The Pattern with the selected line will turn translucent as the line is highlighted in red. \- Click the Avatar Tape on the Avatar. The Pattern will no longer be translucent as the Avatar Tape is highlighted in red. \- When the **Simulation** tool is activated, the selected Pattern outline or Internal Line will attach to the Avatar Tape. **Detach Pattern from Avatar Tape** \- In the 3D window, click the Pattern outline or Internal Line attached to the Avatar Tape. \- Hit the Delete key on the keyboard. The line highlighted in red will return to black. \- When the **Simulation** tool is activated, the Pattern will detach from the Avatar. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to attach and detach patterns from Avatar Tapes in a 3D design environment.

title: Grainline
content: ## **New in 2024.2** **** **List of Content** **Grain Direction** **Link All Colorways** **Grain Orientation** **Grainline Lock** #### **Adjust the direction and orientation of the grainline, while also being able to lock Grainline properties and adjustments across all modes and features within CLO. ** 1. Click the 2D pattern using the ![Transform Pattern On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37931791249049)**Transform Pattern** or ![Edit Pattern On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37931791261337)**Edit Pattern** tool in the 2D toolbar. 2. Adjust the direction and orientation of the grainline in the Property Editor. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37932578723609) ** ** **Grain Direction** | The main angle/ degree for the pattern's placement on the fabric roll. 1) Click the text field. 2) Press the arrow keys on the keyboard to change the degree based on how the Grain Orientation is set up. Examples: • Grain Orientation One way: The numbers will switch every 45 degrees. • Grain Orientation Two Or Four Way: The numbers will switch every 90 Degrees. 3) Or enter a specific degree. ---|--- **Link All Colorways** | If there are multiple colorways within the project file checking this checkbox on will apply the grainline information to all colorways. If the checkbox is unchecked that means each colorway can be different. ****📝****Note:****_This could be helpful if you want more control when entering production or if you are planning on having different fabrics for different colorways._ **Grain ****Orientation** | To decide how many different orientations/ directions the pattern can be placed on the fabric roll. **📝 Note:**_These options are very important for when moving into production and learning how much it would cost to produce the garment. This is also very important because based on the fabric you have applied certain the different orientations will change how much or how little stretch the garment has._ ** One Way ** | The pattern should only be placed in that one orientation that is dictated by the Grain Direction degree. ** Two Way ** | The pattern can be placed in two different orientation. The degree dictated by the Grain Direction and the degree that is the direct opposite (_180 degree from the original_). Examples: • 0 Degree Original: 180 Degree second option. • 90 Degree Original: 270 Degree Second option. ** Four Way ** | The pattern can be placed in four different orientations. The degree dictated by the Grain Direction and any other orientation that 90 degree from the original degree. Examples: • 0 Degree Original: 90,180,270 other options. • 45 Degree Original: 135,225,315 other options. **Grainline Lock** | Checking this on will lock the grainline across all modes of CLO. Stopping any adjustments to the grainline when working with other tools or functions within CLO that can adjust the Grainline. ****📝****Note:****_This locking is very helpful to keep continuity across all of CLO._ _The Print Layout mode and the Edit Texture tools will be the parts of CLO that are affected the most when checking this on or off._ * *
content_description: Discover the new features in CLO 2024.2 that enhance your control over grain direction and orientation, allowing you to lock grainline properties across all modes for seamless garment production.

title: Seam Taping
content: **Reinforce edges of Patterns to withstand from drooping down by gravity when Simulating.** 1. Click on the ![Seam Taping On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37880812122905) **Seam Taping** tool on the 2D toolbar. 2. Select a segment Pattern to reinforce, or Click-and-drag also allows applying seam tapes. 3. Activate the ![Simulation Normal On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37881774490393) **Simulate**. → The seam tape is now being applied to the selected segment and being reinforced. ![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37880795938457) ### ![Label.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/39591676972825) Provide the options for seam tape extension. _****_ 1. Click on the segment with seam tape applied with ![Seam Taping On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37880812122905) **Seam Taping** tool. 2. Set the**Extend** option in the Property Editor. **N****on****e** | Seam tape does not extend. ---|--- **To Outline** | Extend to the pattern outline. **To Seam Taping** | Extend to another seam tape area of ​​the intersected line. * The arrow highlighted on the segment indicates the direction from start to end. ****📝****Note:**** * When extending a seam tape to another seam taping, please make sure there is an intersected seam tape for reference. * If you apply Seam Taping Extend in the lower version (before ver 2024.2), both Start and End are assigned as To Outline in the higher version.
content_description: This page provides a step-by-step guide on how to reinforce pattern edges with seam tape in simulation to prevent drooping due to gravity.

title: Can I cancel my subscription?
content: **Question** Can I cancel my paid subscription? Can I cancel my free trial? **Answer** You can cancel your trial or paid subscription through the [Subscription](https://www.clo3d.com/en/accounts/subscription) section of your account page. Even if you cancel immediately after starting the free trial and regular subscription, you can still use the CLO program until the expiration date. *Please note cancelation of the subscription after the renewal is non-refundable. *Deactivation (remote logout) doesn't cancel your subscription. **Step 1.** Sign in to your account via [clo3d.com](https://clo3d.com/en/) **Step 2.** Navigate to your Subscription page and click the "Cancel Subscription" button. [![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/40475986511257)](https://clo3d.com/en/) **Step 3.** Proceed with the survey for the cancelation reason and click the confirmation button. **Step 4.** Check the Billing section that your subscription expiration date. Please submit an inquiry through our [Contact Us](https://clo3d.com/en/support/contactus) page if you have any questions or difficulties.
content_description: This page provides clear instructions on how to cancel your paid subscription or free trial, ensuring you understand the process and consequences.

title: CLO Fabric Creator
content: **List of Contents** **Open ** **Create Fabric** **Set Options ** **Apply and Save** ### Simply enter your Fabric Type, Composition and Density to quickly create new accurate fabrics within CLO. ### #### **Open** 1. Right-click on the fabric item in Fabric tab in Object browser, then select the Fabric Creator menu. 2. It can also work in Main Menu ▶ Editor ▶ Fabric Creator Menu, and if it work in this way, the created fabric is addded as a new fabric ### #### **Create Fabric** 1. Enter the Name, Supplier, and Owner of the fabric. 2. When selecting the Fabric Type and entering the Composition, the physical properties of the fabric are applied according to the information set and will be previewed. 3. **** Switch ![spanner.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37871925937945) tap to check and modify the physical properties of the fabric as needed. 4. Set the [Material](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/EN/articles/360047317454-%EC%9B%90%EB%8B%A8-%EC%9E%AC%EC%A7%88-%EC%84%A4%EC%A0%95) of the fabric it created, or click the Use CLO Texture Presets option to enable and apply the CLO default textures based on the fabric type. ### ![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37871912285977) ![Label.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/39591556373785) The Composition can be customized based on the selected Fabric Type. 1. Select the Fabric Type 2. Click on the Select menu and then choose the compositions to customize. ![Composition.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37873292933017) * Basic refers to the primary composition used for the selected fabric type, while Additional refers to compositions that can be combined as extras. 3. When entering the composition, the physical properties of the fabric are applied according to the information set and will be previewed. ### #### **Set Options** * **Model** Set the shape to preview the fabric (Cylinder-Circle /Squar, Cape) in the upper left corner of the Fabric Creator window. * **View ** Set the preview to a specified view, or manually adjust to set the desired view in the upper right corner of the fabric Creator window. ****📝****Note:** **Click the Lock button to lock the view adjusted. ### #### **Apply and Save** 1. After the fabric is created, click the Apply and Apply & Close buttons at the bottom. → If the fabric is applied in the 3D garment, the results can be checked right away. → The Fabric Creator window is closed simultaneously as it is applied as the property of the fabric. 2. Or, click the Save button to save the created fabric as a file. (ZFAB).
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for users to efficiently create, customize, and save fabric types in CLO by entering specific details and adjusting physical properties.

title: Set Color Theme
content: **New in CLO 2024.2. ** Set the theme to Dark or Light based on your preference and environment. **Dark theme** uses a dark background for the user interface, reducing eye strain and glare, especially in low-light environments. It helps to keep the overall brightness of the screen lower, which can be more comfortable during prolonged use. **Light theme** , on the other hand, features a bright background that provides a clean and crisp appearance, improving readability in well-lit environments. **** 1. Click on the **Setting » User Settings** in the menu bar. 2. Set the theme under **User Interface > Appearance**. ** ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37041977442841) ****** 3. Restart CLO to apply the theme.
content_description: Discover how to customize your CLO 2024.2 experience by selecting between Dark and Light themes for optimal comfort and readability in any environment.

title: Low-Res Garment
content: **List of Conetents** Low-Res Garment Low-Res Garment Settings **Low-Res Garment ** \- Decrease general quality of the 3D Garment. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022475628/mceclip0.png) **Low-Res Garment** tool from the 3D toolbar or navigate and select Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ **Low-Res Garment.** ** Low-Res Garment Settings ** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022475648/mceclip1.png) **Low-Res Garment** tool from the 3D toolbar and the Low-Res Properties window will appear. * **Particle Distance** \- Change all Patterns’ Particle Distance to 20mm. \- Modify **Tolerance** to decide the range of Particle Distance so that only Patterns with corresponding Particle Distance value will be affected. Patterns with Particle Distance value outside of the **Tolerance** will not be affected. The default **Tolerance** range is 5mm to 20mm. * **Add’l Thickness - Collision** \- Change all Patterns’ Add’l Thickness- Collision to the default value, 2.5mm. \- Modify **Tolerance** to decide the range of Add’l Thickness- Collision so that only Patterns with corresponding Add’l Thickness - Collision value will be affected. Patterns with Add’l Thickness - Collision value outside of the Tolerance will not be affected. ** ** * **Skin Offset ** \- Change all Avatar’s Skin Offset to the default value, 3mm. \- Modify **Tolerance** to decide the range of Skin Offset so that only Patterns with corresponding Skin Offset value will be affected. Patterns with Skin Offset value outside of the Tolerance will not be affected. * **Simulation Quality** \- Change the Simulation preset to the default setting, NORMAL. \- To decrease the general quality of the 3D Garment only with the desired options, toggle off options as needed. \- Select OK. The **Simulation** icon will change. \- Activate the **Simulation** to apply the settings. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to adjust low-resolution garment settings in 3D garment design software for optimized performance and quality control.

title: Reset 3D Arrangement (All)
content: **Reset 3D Arrangement（All）** **** \- Re-arrange 3D Patterns prior to the Simulation. \- Use the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022651728/mceclip1.png) **Reset 3D Arrangement(All)** tool when Garments are not properly draped after arranging them in the 3D window. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022651728/mceclip1.png) **Reset 3D Arrangement(All)** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select 3D Garment ▶ **Reset 3D Arrangement(All). ** \- All Patterns will be re-arranged in the 3D window prior to the Simulation.
content_description: The "Reset 3D Arrangement (All)" page provides a quick guide to re-arranging 3D patterns for optimal garment draping before simulation.

title: Reset 2D Arrangement (All)
content: **Reset 2D Arrangement（All）** **** **-** Re-Arrange 3D Patterns according to the Pattern Arrangement in the 2D window. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022651688/mceclip0.png) **Reset 2D Arrangement（All)** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select 3D Garment ▶ **Reset 2D Arrangement (All).** \- All Patterns will be re-arranged in the 3D window reflecting the Pattern Arrangement in the 2D window.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to provide instructions for using the "Reset 2D Arrangement (All)" tool to align 3D patterns with their corresponding arrangement in the 2D window.

title: Pleats
content: **Objective** Create the desired shape of pleats to Patterns. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Pleats ▶ **Pleats**** **2D Toolbar ▶**![Pleats.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360059605713/Pleats.png) Pleats** **** **Operation** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. ** ** 2. Click to create a start point and an endpoint of a reference line of the pleats along Pattern Outlines. → A Pattern is divided into two. 3. Click on the side where the pleats will be added. → The Pleats window appears. 4. Configure the options and select OK. **Pleats Type** | Select the type of the pleats (Knife, Box, or Accordion). ---|--- ** Specification ** | Number of Pleats | Decide the number of pleats. Depth | Assign the depth of the pleats (the depth of folded pleats). Interval | Set the interval between pleats when there are two or more pleats. Create Notch | Select where to create Notch (Both, Start, or End). Reverse Direction | Reverse the direction where the pleats will be added. **Option** | Assign fold angles to the fold lines. Greater the difference between the angle of Outside Fold and Inside Fold, sharper the folds are. → The pleats are created on the Pattern. → If there is an Internal Line in the Pattern, it is also moved and rotated along with the Pattern. (ver 6.0) **※ Note: **If the segment where pleats to be created is sewn to another Pattern, the pleats will be automatically sewn. If the segment is not sewn, use the [Pleats Sewing](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000307468-%ED%94%8C%EB%A6%AC%EC%B8%A0-%EC%A0%91%EA%B8%B0-%EC%9E%AC%EB%B4%89) tool to sew the pleats to the other Pattern.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for creating and customizing pleats on patterns using the 2D Pattern tool in Clo3D.

title: Fold Arrangement
content: **List of Contents** Fold Arrangement Fold Patterns Check Fold Angle Sync Fold Arrangement Angle **Fold Arrangement** \- Fold Patterns based on internal lines and sewing lines in the 3D window. \- Select the **Fold Arrangement** tool ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022454608/mceclip0.png) from the 3D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select 3D Garment ▶ **Fold Arrangement** ** Fold Patterns** \- To use the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022454608/mceclip0.png) **Fold Arrangement** tool，there must be fiducial lines such as Internal Lines and Sewing Lines on Patterns. \- Click on the Internal Line or the Sewing Line which the Pattern will fold base on. \- When the **Gizmo** tool appears, click and drag to fold the Pattern towards the desired direction. **Check Fold Angle** \- The **Fold Angle** of the selected Internal Line or the Sewing Line will change automatically and will be reflected in the Property Editor. \- Fold the Pattern with the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022454608/mceclip0.png) **Fold Arrangement** tool and check the **Fold Angle**. \- To create a crisp fold, adjust the **Fold Angle** to 0 or 360 as desired. ** Sync Fold Arrangement Angle_ver4.2.0** \- Toggle on or off Sync Fold Arrangement Angle \- Navigate to Main Menu ▶ Settings ▶ User Settings ▶ 3D ▶ Arragement \- Toggle off the Sync Fold Arrangement Angle option. \- The Fold Angle is not changed when Pattern is fold with the**![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022454608/mceclip0.png) Fold Arrangement **tool.** ** Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide to using the Fold Arrangement tool in 3D garment design, detailing the process of creating and adjusting fold patterns and angles.

title: Copy/Paste/Replace
content: ### **List of Contents** #### **Copy and Paste** #### **Replace** #### Depending on the user's needs, copy and paste patterns or replace them only in the form of a specific pattern while maintaining the original properties. ### #### **Copy and Paste** 1. Click the ![Transform Pattern On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37879877879705)**Transform Pattern** or ![Edit Pattern On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37879877892633)E**dit Pattern tool** on the 2D toolbar. 2. Right-click on the pattern or Internal line to be copied. 3. Click the **Copy** (Ctrl+C) menu. 4. **Right-click on the 2D background and click the Paste **(Ctrl+V) menu. 5. Press the Shift key to place it on a vertical/horizontal/45˚ line or freely click anywhere you want. **📝****Note:** * Right-clicking during paste allows you to enter values for Interval/Number of Shapes/Position (Internal Line). * Patterns can be copied and pasted even between multi-run CLO programs. #### #### **Replace** 1. Right-click on the original pattern to be replaced. 2. Click the **Replace** menu. → The pattern is replaced with the copied pattern's segment point locations, curves, notches, baselines, pattern names, and grading information. → Sewing lines, Internal shapes, Graphics, Fabrics, Topstitching, Puckering, and buttons are maintained as the properties of the original pattern. **📝****Note:** Pattern replacement is only possible if the number of Segment points is the same. ![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37879877900697) ### _**![Label.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37879893509529)**_ _****_ Even if the old and new patterns have different segment points, you can easily replace them. 1. Right-click on the original pattern, internal line, internal shape, baseline, or baseline shape to be replaced. 2. Click **Replaced by** menu. → The original pattern or line is replaced with the new one's segment point locations, curves, notches, baselines, pattern names, and grading information. → Sewing lines, Internal shapes, Graphics, Fabrics, Topstitching, Puckering, and buttons are maintained as the properties of the original pattern. 3. Select the new pattern, internal line, internal shape, baseline, or baseline shape. → W**hen the number of segment points is the**same** , t**he replacement process will be completed automatically. 4. Click and match the Segment point from the original pattern to the new pattern. **→** W**hen the number of segment points**differs** , the Segment point matching action is required. → ****After matching enough Segment points,****t** he replacement process will be completed automatically. 5. **Press the**Enter** key to complete if enough core points have been matched or if there are no more points to match.** **📝 Note:** * If both the original and new patterns are half-symmetry, their center points will automatically align. * **For unclosed****internal shapes or baseline shapes, their endpoints are automatically matched. ** * **Press the Delete to cancel the last step, or****Press the Esc key to cancel all actions** Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to efficiently copy, paste, and replace patterns in CLO3D while preserving original properties.

title: Freeze/Unfreeze
content: **Objective** Use this function to fasten patterns like solid objects. Deactivated patterns do not collide during simulation, however, frozen patterns do (they maintain collision). Therefore, it is better to use for draping multiple layered garments. For instance, draping and freezing inner garments first, then draping outerwear above helps avoid occasional instabilities. **Location** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005490267/Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png) **Select/Move** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005490287/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Transform.png) **Transform Pattern** **Operation** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated above. 2. Right-click on the 3D or 2D pattern and click **Freeze/Unfreeze.** → The pattern selected is frozen/unfrozen. **※Note:** Right-click in the empty space of the 3D window and hover over **Show/Hide Color** , then click******Show Freeze** to show or hide the color applied during freeze. (ver 6.1)
content_description: This web page provides instructions for using the 'Freeze/Unfreeze' function to efficiently manage pattern collisions while draping layered garments in 3D simulations.

title: Convert to Curve Point
content: **Easily convert Segment Points on the patterns to Curve Points, or Curve Points to Segment Points** **** 1. Right-click on the segment point with ![Edit Pattern On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/40166904035609) **Edit Pattern** tool or on the curve point with ![Edit Curve Point On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/40166914856217)**Edit Curve Point** tool. 2. Click the **Convert to Curve Point**. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Maintain Curve** | Convert selected points by automatically adding curve points to maintain the curvature. If the segment is already smooth enough, no curved points will added. **Convert Only** | ![Label.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/40166904041881) Convert selected points without adding curve points. The segment result may be affected slightly. **📝****Note:** Clicking while holding down the Shift key on the keyboard allows for multiple selections.
content_description: Easily convert between Segment Points and Curve Points on patterns with simple right-click options to enhance your design flexibility.

title: Open MetaHuman Body Types
content: ### **Objective** Select a desired MetaHuman body type and create an outfit for your MetaHuman in CLO before bringing the outfit to Unreal Engine as USD files. ### **Location** Library ▶ Click Avatar Folder ▶ MetaHuman ▶ Double click to download a desired MetaHuman body types ## **※ Note :** * Arms need to be bent on export in order for Unreal Engine's USD import pipeline to work properly. Once garments are ready to be exported, apply a pose named 'Default_Pose' in Pose folder to a desired MetaHuman body. * A pose named 'Apose' is provided in order for garments to be fit on a desired MetaHuman body with ease, especially around arms. * In Marvelous Designer versions below 2024.0.173, applying the two aforementioned poses to a MetaHuman body will result in the error message "No matching avatar" and will not be applied.
content_description: This web page guides users in selecting a MetaHuman body type and designing an outfit in CLO, ensuring proper export to Unreal Engine as USD files with specific pose instructions for optimal garment fitting.

title: 3D State
content: **Record 3D state to compare or check your design process. ** 1. Open the History window on the left side of CLO. 2. Click the ![3D State.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/38099405049753) **Add 3D State** button to record 3D state as a project file. ![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/38099374825497) ### ![Label_Final.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/38099374826393) Preview the 3D state by hovering over the 3D state before opening it. ![3D State.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/38099939408409) ![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/38099374825497) 3. Double click the 3D state to open. 4. Right-click on the 3D state to rename, delete or add. **📝****Note:** When you save a project file(ZPRJ), the 3D State file is also saved with it. The more 3D files that are saved, the bigger the file is. It may slow down the speed when you open and save the file.
content_description: This webpage provides a step-by-step guide on how to record and manage 3D states in CLO to effectively compare and evaluate your design process.

title: Edit Sewing
content: **List of Contents** Edit Sewing Select Sewing Move Sewing Adjust Sewing Length Sewing Line Pop-Up Menu **Edit Sewing** \- Select and edit Sewing Lines in the 2D window. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022128067/mceclip0.png) **Edit Sewing** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select Sewing ▶ **Edit Sewing.** ** Select Sewing** \- With the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022128067/mceclip0.png) **Edit Sewing** tool selected, click on the Sewing Line to be selected. \- The sewing Line will be bolded. \- When there are multiple Sewing Lines on the selected Pattern outline, pop-up menu showing all Sewing Line options will appear. \- Use the color chip in front of the Sewing Line name to choose the desired one. \- The Sewing Lines are ordered in an ascending order, arranging the latest to last. **Move Sewing** \- Select and drag the center of the Sewing Line. \- When the selected Sewing Line is on a symmetric Pattern, the second half of the Sewing Line on its symmetric pair will be moved simultaneously. **Adjust Sewing Length** * **Adjust Freely ** \- Select and drag one end point of the Sewing Line towards the desired direction. \- Only the selected half of the Sewing Line will be adjusted. To match the sewing length of the second half of the Sewing Line, repeat the same process as above. When adjusting the second half of the Sewing Line, a blue point will appear guiding the length of the first half of the Sewing Line. * **Adjust with Designated Value ** \- Select and drag one end point of the Sewing Line towards the desired direction. \- While holding down the mouse, right-click to access the Moving Distance window. \- Enter the desired distance the point will be moved. **Sewing Line Pop-Up Menu** * **Access Right Click Pop-Up Menu ** \- Right-click on the Sewing Line to be edited to access the pop-up menu. * **Select All with Same Property** \- Use this option to select all Sewing Lines with the same property. * **Fold Strength ** \- Select all Sewing Lines with the same Fold Strength value. * **Fold Angle ** \- Select all Sewing Lines with the same Fold Angle value. * **Reverse Sewing ** \- Reverse the direction notch of the selected Sewing Line. * **Delete Sewing **\- Delete the selected Sewing Line. \- Right-click on the Sewing Line and select **Delete Sewing.** \- When deleting a Sewing Line, its pair will be deleted as well. \- Use this option when directional notches are twisted. * **Merge ** \- Merge Patterns based on the selected Sewing Line. * **Add Point to Pattern on Start/ Add Point to Pattern on End ** \- Add points to the Pattern outline based on the start or the end point of the Sewing Line. \- The point near the directional notch is the start point and the point far from the directional notch is the end point. * **Deactivate Sewing (Selected) **\- Deactivate Sewing Lines to disable their functions. \- When the selected Sewing Line is deactivated, it will turn white. \- When the Simulation is activated, the Patterns with the deactivated Sewing Line will no longer sewn to each other. \- To activate the Sewing Line again, right click on the Sewing Line and select **Activate Sewing.** * **Hide Sewing ** \- Hide Sewing Lines in the 2D window. \- When the Sewing Lines are hidden, they will no longer appear in the 2D window. \- To show them again, right click on the Sewing Line and select **Show Sewing (All).** Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for managing and editing sewing lines within the 2D design interface, detailing tools and actions for selecting, moving, adjusting, and customizing sewing line properties.

title: [View Control] Zoom In/Out, Rotation
content: **Objective** In CLO, the mouse wheel and the right button can be used to zoom in, zoom out, and rotate the screen. The Maya and 3Ds Max view control methods are also supported alongside the default view control method and interface can be modified as needed and use differently. ** Operation** **Move![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001788308/3D_Pan.png)** ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001762547/17______.png) Hold down the mouse wheel and drag to move the screen. If you are using Mac's Magic Mouse, please hold down the Alt key on the keyboard and click-and-drag the left mouse key. **Zoom In/Out![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001762587/3D_Zoom.png)** ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001762567/18______.png) Scroll down (zoom in) and up (zoom out) the mouse wheel to zoom in and zoom out the screen. Or, hold down Alt Key on the keyboard and the left button of the mouse simultaneously and drag up (zoom out) or down (zoom in). **※ Note:** Zoom in or zoom out using the + (zoom in) and - (zoom out) keys on the keyboard (ver2.4.0.) **Rotate![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001788288/3D_Rotate.png)** ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001788328/19___________.png) Hold down the right button of the mouse and drag to rotate the 3D window.
content_description: Discover how to effectively navigate and manipulate the 3D environment in CLO using mouse controls for movement, zooming, and rotation.

title: How can I export FBX from CLO to APEXFiz?
content: **Question** I would like to know the recommended menu settings for FBX eport in CLO in order to use [Extract Patterns]. **Answer** [Extract Patterns] is a function that is only supported by the 3D OPTION of APEXFIz. Below is a menu of CLO software. ![FBX from CLO to APEXFiz.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/40661188216601) * Select necessary avatar and patterns. * Select multiple object, not single object. Export without combining vertex * Select [Thin] for thickness. * Select default [mm] for scale. * If textures are required, select embed media. * If textures are required, enter a file name and a folder name with half-width characters. * Create a unified UV map. At this time, all pattern UVs should be arranged within the 0-1 space in the UV editor, ensuring there is no overlap. Place the pattern UVs according to the knitting direction in APEXFiz, as this direction cannot be changed in the Extract Pattern menu. Textures with alpha(hair, eyelash, etc.) may not be imported correctly. Internal lines(design lines) cannot be imported. Stitch data will not be readable in APEXFiz.
content_description: This web page provides essential guidance on the optimal FBX export settings from CLO for utilizing the Extract Patterns feature in APEXFiz.

title: What is CLO Verified?
content: ### CLO OFFICIAL VERIFICATION CLO Verified is not a training, but an assessment of your skills in CLO Available for any CLO user with an Active Individual or Student License. No Enterprise Licenses can be used The test is broken into 3 different parts 1. Build a garment from a DXF pattern. 2. Correct a built garment that needs to be fixed/edited [similar to what you would be tasked with working in the industry]. 3. Combine the 2 garments to create a full look which you will render in CLO. A Visual Quality Standards document will be sent the week before the test that will provide you with guidelines for the project submission. You will receive all tech packs, patterns, and necessary materials the day of the test for all 3 parts. Once completed, you will be notified 2-3 weeks after the test by email. You will receive both the outcome (Pass/Fail) and feedback about the files you have submitted. ### CERTIFICATE & BADGE All participants who pass the test will receive the CLO Verified Certificate, the only CLO recognized certificate, as well as the CLO Verified Badge which can be added to LinkedIn or other social media to show others their proven level of CLO expertise. ### PRACTICE ASSESSMENT We recommend all users take the self-graded Practice Test before signing up and paying for the Official Verification. This test is very similar but slightly shorter than the Official Verification and includes a Visual Quality Standards Guide to help you. Passing the CLO Verified Practice Test does not guarantee that you will pass the Official Verification, but it does mean that you should possess the skills needed to do so. Also, passing the practice test does not make you CLO Verified. To become CLO Verified you must take and Pass the Official Verification which the CLO Academic Team reviews and grades. ### ****CURRENTLY THE CLO VERIFIED PRACTICE & OFFICIAL VERIFICATION ARE ONLY AVAILABLE IN ENGLISH**** ### THINK YOU’RE READY? * Do you use CLO regularly [15+ hours a week] with a focus on the CLO garment construction workflow? * Are you able to quickly troubleshoot issues within CLO? * Are you comfortable with Tech-Packs and Visual Quality Standards? To sign up for the Waitlist for alerts about upcoming tests and/or take the Practice Assessment please head over to the CLO Academy [HERE](https://www.cloacademy.online/catalog)
content_description: The CLO Official Verification webpage aims to assess and certify your skills in CLO through a structured test, providing a recognized certificate and badge for those who pass, while also offering a practice assessment to help prepare candidates.

Go through the courses entirely, especially the INTRO TO CLO Courses. The instructors review the Quizzes and Submissions and adjust grading accordingly. _***CLO has a no-refund policy. Use of or access to CLO Academy Online in any way confirms your acceptance of our refund policy* **_ **FAQ** _There are a lot of courses/resources online, but it’s hard to figure out what’s best for me._ * CLO Academy is a centralized, comprehensive learning experience that guides users through their CLO journey like a proper university program. * It’s taught in the way that we, at CLO, believe it should be learned - from years of experience training enterprise users, academics, and individuals. This is how you should learn CLO if you are interested in using it professionally. * We want to ensure that those using CLO are using it correctly; we’ve found that even users who consider themselves intermediate/experienced may not know how to do everything the best way. _I looked at fashion school courses but they were too expensive._ * We tried to make CLO Academy as affordable as possible while providing the highest level of quality and support for our learners. _I just want a place where I can learn everything, step by step, and ask questions if I get stuck._ * With CLO Academy, you can follow a guided curriculum that you know you can trust, without having to search through tons of unverified courses online. Our instructors and support team are also available to assist you with any questions or challenges you face. _I’m already an experienced user, how can I validate my credentials?_ * [CLO Verified](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/40015910802585-What-is-CLO-Verified) was developed in response to frequent requests from our individual users. Unlike courses on other platforms, these credentials are verified by CLO designers and include official CLO branding. _I’m not seeing any courses I’m interested in._ * Listening to our community is key, and we’re committed to releasing more content designed for the ever-evolving needs of the industry. You can expect to see more courses on topics based on your feedback. _Where do I ask questions, if I have them?_ * Learners can message the instructor directly in the Journal or via messages with the course. * We have a dedicated Discord channel for learners. ([How can I join CLO Discord?](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/7814962429977-How-can-I-join-CLO-Discord)) * You can also reach us at [cloacademy@clo3d.com](mailto:cloacademy@clo3d.com) for any CLO Academy related questions.

title: What languages does CLO come in?
content: **Question** What languages does CLO come in? **Answer** We currently offer CLO in English, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Spanish, French, Italian, Portuguese, and much more. To change your language settings in CLO, go to Language in Settings, select the desired language, then restart the program to apply the changes. The manuals and video buttons connected within the CLO program may not be available in the set language. If you wish to change the language of the YouTube tutorial videos to your preferred language, you can first enable subtitles and then view them with automatic translation in your desired language. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/40265359237017) Additionally, you can check tutorials on the dedicated CLO YouTube channels available in Portuguese, Spanish, and Japanese. * CLO Portuguese Youtube: [Here](https://www.youtube.com/@CLOBrasil) * CLO Spanish Youtube: [Here](https://www.youtube.com/@CLOesp) * CLO Japanese Youtube: [Here](https://www.youtube.com/@CLOJapan)

title: Render Output Improvement (Graininess, Noise)
content: **Where to Start** Once your garment or look is finished, make sure you use the [Hi-Res Garment tool](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115012380608-Hi-Res-Garment) and simulate to see the realistic drape. Next, go to the **Render Menu ▶ Render** to enter the [Render Mode](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115014784747-Run-V-Ray-Render). Click to start an Interactive Render. As you view the preview, a good place to start is to use the default settings; ● set up the image size as desired ● use a **plain background** (with an image vignette if desired) ● **PNG file format** is lossless and will therefore give you better quality than the JPEG ● reset the lighting to Default (**Studio Low Contrast**) & activate **ground shadow** (this effect is a must when rendering a full avatar) ● **Windows** users: use the **GPU Engine** ● Noise Threshold set at **0.05** ● Max Render Time = **20 min** ● Light & Material Quality at **Medium** If you start here and create a final render, stop Interactive Render and click Final Render. Watch this complete and take note how long it takes. From here, you can make adjustments to the lighting and render properties to improve the image quality. **Further Considerations** Creating a beautiful image in CLO can be tricky at times. You need to balance the complexity of your project with the limitations of your hardware and the amount of time your computer will take to give you the final result. Here are a few things to consider; ● **How does your hardware match up to our[system requirements](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000307168-CLO-system-requirements-March-2024)?** It is better to go towards the _Recommended_ rather than _Minimum_. If your computer matches the minimum requirements, yes, it may work, but it will not be a good experience. You will quickly run into speed limitations not only while rendering, but with simulating as your garments get more complex. The amount of RAM in your computer will make the biggest difference with speed. ● **What materials did you use?** Are there any metals, sparkles, shiny areas on the fabrics, buttons, zippers, snaps, etc.? Anything that will reflect light while rendering can add more time to the rendering process. ● **Have you added accessories or objects in the scene that have glass or metal?** Did you create a “mirror” or place a ground plane that is very shiny? Think about your environment. It may be awesome to have a detailed room around your avatar and garment, but opting for a simple, plain background will not only reduce rendering time, but also focus the viewer’s attention on the garment. ● **How complex is the garment or garments making up the looks?** Is there visible internal layers or multiple layered garments? Are you using lots of buttons, zippers, graphics, prints, etc.? Is there puckering or have you activated Realistic Seamline while using the Fill tool? ● **What image size are you using?** It is recommended you pick from the pixel size options (640 x 480, etc.) as this will reduce the rendering time. The paper size layouts may seem attractive but the document/pixel ratios can cause a slowing of the rendering process. If needed, changing the resolution (ppi) will slow down the rendering process. ● **Check your[Render Properties](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115014899148-Edit-V-Ray-Render-Properties):** ○ Are you rendering **fur**? It is recommended to switch to CPU Engine to get better results, **but** it will take longer. So you need to decide whether the slower rendering is beneficial. ○ What is your **Noise Threshold**? Default 0.05, the lower you go, the better the details **but** it will take longer. ○ **Max Render Time** ; Based on all the variables, CLO will do the best it can with the time you have allotted. ○ **Light** and **Material Quality** will also affect the length of your render. **※****Note: **If you want to render an animation (rather than capturing the 3D window), always do a single render to start. The time it took to render that one image should be multiplied by the number of frames in the animation. ● Example: ○ image rendering time = 5 minutes ○ frames in animation = 450 ○ how long the render animation will take: 2250 minutes or 37.5 hours (a day and a half)
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide to effectively rendering garments in CLO, providing essential steps and considerations for achieving high-quality images with optimal settings and hardware.

title: Select Mesh (Box)
content: **List of Contents** Select Mesh (Box) Select Multiple Areas Delete Selection Invert Selection Select a Segment Select a Pattern **Select Mesh (Box) ** \- Select and move 3D Garment Mesh as needed. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022721948/mceclip0.png) **Select Mesh****(Box)** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select 3D Garment ▶ **Select Mesh (Box)** ** Select Multiple Areas ** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022721948/mceclip0.png) **Select Mesh (Box)** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Patterns in the 2D window and 3D window will appear in yellow-green Mesh structure. \- Click and drag on the Pattern to create marquee box to select desired area. \- Hold down the Shift and Ctrl keys on the keyboard to select multiple areas on the 3D Garment. **Delete ** \- To deselect particular areas, hold down the Ctrl key on the keyboard and click and drag to encompass the desired area in the 2D window. The encompassed area will be deselected. **Invert Selection ** \- To invert the selection, hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to click and drag on the 3D Garment. \- The areas originally not selected will be selected and vice-versa. \- The selected area will be highlighted in yellow-green. **Select a Segment ** \- Double click on the Pattern outline in the 2D or 3D window to select a segment. **Select a Pattern ** \- Double click within the Pattern in the 2D or 3D window to select a Pattern. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on using selection tools for manipulating 3D garment mesh in the CLO 3D design software.

title: Zipper
content: **List of Contents** Zipper Creating Zipper Unzip/Zip Zipper Edit Zipper Tape/ Slider Property Zipper Tape/ Slider Right-Click Pop-Up Menu **Zipper** \- Create and express zippers easily and quickly. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022759807/mceclip0.png) **Zipper** tool from the 3D toolbar. ** ****Creating Zipper** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022759807/mceclip0.png) **Zipper** tool from the 3D toolbar and navigate to the 3D window. \- The Pattern outlines and Internal Lines on the 3D Garment will appear as dashed lines. \- Hover the mouse over the Pattern outlines or Internal Lines where the Zipper will be placed. \- Click once and drag the mouse cursor along the Pattern outline or Internal Line. \- Double click to complete the first half of the Zipper. \- Hover the mouse over the Pattern outlines or Internal Lines where the other half of the Zipper will be placed. \- Repeat the same procedure. A blue dot will appear to guide the length of the first half of the Zipper. \- When the Zipper is established, the Zipper tape and the Zipper slider will appear along the designated Pattern outlines or Internal Lines. \- The Zipper slider will always be located at the starting position where Zipper was placed \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022760867/mceclip1.png) **Simulation** from the 3D Toolbar. \- The Zipper will fasten. **Unzip/ Zip Zipper** \- With Simulation off, select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022760907/mceclip2.png) **Select/Move** tool from the 3D toolbar to partially unzip or Zip the Zipper. \- Click on the Zipper slider, and it will be highlighted in yellow. \- Click and drag the Zipper slider along the Zipper tape. A grey slider will follow along the mouse to preview the location. \- Release the mouse to finalize Zipper slider’s location. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022760867/mceclip1.png) **Simulation** from the 3D toolbar. \- Only the designated part of the Zipper will fasten or unfasten. **Editing Zipper Tape/ Slider Property** \- Use the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022760907/mceclip2.png) **Select/Move** tool from the 3D toolbar to select either the Zipper tape or the Zipper slider. * **Zipper Tape ** * **Width (MM) ** \- Type in a specific value to assign width to the Zipper tape. ** ** * **Thickness (MM) ** \- Type in a specific value to assign thickness to the Zipper tape. \- Change the Garment Rendering Style to ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022824148/mceclip4.png) **Thick Textured Surface** to see Zipper tape’s thickness. * **Fasten Zipper** \- Toggle on/off the option to completely Zip or unzip the Zipper. \- Toggle Off the **Fasten Zipper** option to unzip the zipper. * **Material - Texture** \- Change the texture of the Zipper tape. \- Add Normal Map and check on/off **Desaturation** to convert the texture into greyscale. * **Material - Color** \- Change the color of the Zipper tape. \- Adjust **Ambient Intensity** and **Diffuse Intensity** as needed. **Ambient Intensity** expresses the effect of ambient light. **Diffuse Intensity** controls the intensity of the applied texture image and color. \- Adjust **Specular Colo** r as needed. With the **Shininess** option, modify the sheen of the Zipper tape. \- Add Specular Map to assign how **Specular Color** is applied to the Zipper slider. \- Adjust **Emission Color** to set the color that emits from the Zipper tape. * **Fold** -**Strength:** set the strength of the fold of the Sewing Line between the Pattern and the Zipper. \- **Angle** : set the fold angle between the Zipper and the Pattern to express the fold . * **Particle Distance(mm)** \- Adjust Particle Distance for Zipper Tapes(ver4.1.0). * **Zipper Slider ** * **Shape ** \- Choose the design of the Zipper slider. * **Size** \- Select the size of the Zipper slider from the provided presets, or type in a desired percentage to adjust manually. * **Fasten Zipper** \- Completely Zip or unzip the Zipper. \- Toggle On/Off the **Reverse Zipper Direction** option to locate the Zipper pull at either end of the Zipper. \- Toggle On/Off the **Move to Opposite Side** option to attach the Zipper pull to either half of the Zipper tape when the Zipper is unzipped. * **Material** \- Adjust provided options to add texture or colors to the Zipper slider. \- Adjust the **Opacity** to express the Zipper slider as translucent or solid. **Zipper Tape/ Slider Right-Click Pop-Up Menu** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022760907/mceclip2.png) **Select/Move** tool from the 2D toolbar and navigate to 2D window. \- Right click on the Zipper tape/ slider to be edited. \- The pop-up menu with options below will appear. * **Zipper Tape** * **Delete** \- Delete the Zipper tape and slider. \- Select the Zipper seam line, right-click and select **Delete.** \- Or, Select the Zipper seam line, and hit the Delete Key on the Keyboard. * **Reverse (Right Clicked)** \- Similar to the Free Sewing tool, both halves of the Zipper tape need to be established in the same direction. If they are sewn incorrectly, the Zipper tape may twist. \- If Zipper appears to be deformed during Simulation, right-click and select **Reverse** to reverse the Sewing Line. * **Flip Normal (Right Clicked Teeth) ** \- Flip the fabric side of the Zipper tape in the 3D window. \- Select the Zipper Sewing Line, right-click and select **Flip Normal.** * **Deactivate/Freeze** \- Deactivate or Freeze the selected Zipper tape to fix and exclude the selected Zipper from Simulation. \- Right-click on Zipper seam line, select **Deactivate** or **Freeze.** \- To Reactivate or Unfreeze the deactivated/frozen Zipper tape, right-click the Zipper seam line again and select **Reactivate** or **Unfreeze.** * **Zipper Slider ** * **Delete -**Delete the Zipper Tape and Slider. \- Select the Zipper seam line, right-click and select **Delete.** \- Or, Select the Zipper seam line, and hit the Delete Key on the Keyboard. * **Deactivate/Freeze ****-** Deactivate or Freeze the selected Zipper Pull to fix and exclude the selected Zipper from Simulation. \- Right-click on Zipper Slider, select **Deactivate** or **Freeze.** Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for creating, editing, and managing zippers in a 3D garment design environment.

title: Non-testable Fabrics for CLO Fabric Digitization Service
content: **Fabric Type** | **Physical Properties Testing** | **3D Image Scanning** | **Comments** ---|---|---|--- Short Fur | O | X | Short Fur can be expressed by setting the Fur option for the Material type of CLO Fabric. Long Fur | X | X | Long Fur can be expressed by setting the Fur option for the Material type of CLO Fabric. Feather Yarns | X | X | The decorations on the fabric make it difficult to measure stretch and bending accurately. Foil | O | X | Foil can be expressed by setting the Iridescene option for the material type of CLO Fabric. PVC | O | X | PVC can be expressed by setting the Iridescene option for the material type of CLO Fabric. Glitter | O | X | Glitter can expressed by setting the Glitter option for the material type of CLO fabric. Sequin | X | X | Sequin can be expressed using CLO. Pleats | X | X | Pleated fabric can be created by using CLO. Elastic Band | X | X | The unavailability of a suitable swatch size makes it difficult to measure physical properties. Wide Stripe Fabric (Made of different yarns) | X | X | The combination of the multiple properties makes it difficult to measure physical properties accurately in a single fabric. Dangling Embellishments | X | X | The decorations on the fabric make it difficult to measure stretch and bending accurately. Complicated Novelty Yarns | X | X | The decorations on the fabric make it difficult to measure stretch and bending accurately. Multi-layer Fabric | X | X | If the multiple fabric layers are only partially attached, it can affect the accuracy of physical property measurements. Crinkled Fabric | X | X | Fabric with processed crinkles is difficult to measure its stretch accurately. Openwork Lace | X | X | Fabric with a very loose weave is difficult to measure its stretch and bending properties.
content_description: This web page provides an overview of various fabric types, their physical properties testing challenges, and the use of 3D image scanning in CLO Fabric applications.

title: Register API Plug-In
content: ### **Objective** By using [CLO API](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360017616633), develop and add customized features to CLO. For example, develop a feature to collect necessary BOM information from a 3D garment produced in CLO. Then, add and use the customized feature in CLO. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ Settings ▶ User Settings ▶ **CLO API** ** Operation** 1. Follow the path indicated below: Main Menu ▶ Settings ▶ User Settings ▶ **CLO API** 2. Click the ![plus_button.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360019478214) **Add** button on the right top corner. → A File Explorer dialog appears where you can search *.dll or *.dylib files. 3. Select and **Open** the desired *.dll or *.dylib file. → The Register Plug-In window appears. 4. Refer to below and configure an UI for the plug-in to be added. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Name** | Name the plug-in. **Position** | Main Menu, child menus for the selected Main Menu, and any additional corresponding child menus appear in order. Select a desired menu and choose the plug-in's position in terms of the selected menu. 5. Click **OK** to complete the registration. ※Note: * Registered plug-ins also appear in below path: Main Menu ▶ Settings ▶ **Plug-in ** * Please [Contact Us,](https://www.clo3d.com/contact) if you have any questions.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for developing and adding customized features to CLO using the CLO API, including how to register plug-ins for enhanced functionality.
